items.title: From Campbell’s to Conagra, food industry warns of price hikes
items.summary: Major food companies like Conagra, Campbell's, and McCormick are warning of impending price hikes on their products due to sustained increases in energy, fertilizer costs, tariffs, and potential impacts from the El Niño weather pattern. Executives state that cost-cutting measures are no longer sufficient to offset inflation, forcing them to raise prices to maintain profit margins. This trend will likely put further pressure on consumers and has implications for the broader economy and political landscape.

items.title: Hooker Furnishings Reports Second Quarter Results
items.summary: Hooker Furnishings reported its fiscal 2027 second quarter results, highlighting significant tariff recoveries that positively impacted operating income, despite a decrease in consolidated net sales. The company achieved its third consecutive quarter of profitability, driven by tariff recoveries, cost reductions, and growth in specific segments like private-label and outdoor furnishings. While consumer demand remains challenging, Hooker Furnishings is encouraged by strengthening backlog and commitments for its Margaritaville product line, expecting improved results in the second half of fiscal 2027.

items.title: Booking Sees Resilient Travel Demand, Touts AI-Powered Connected Trip Growth
items.summary: Booking Holdings Inc. experienced resilient travel demand in Q2, with bookings strengthening from June as Middle East conflict concerns eased. The company's AI-powered Connected Trip strategy is gaining traction, representing a low double-digit share of transactions and growing faster than individual bookings. Booking is also focusing on efficiency, identifying $100 million in savings and reducing customer-service costs, while repurchasing $7.3 billion in stock during the first half of the year.

items.title: The Manufacturers Life Insurance Company Sells 24,403 Shares of The Kroger Co. $KR
items.summary: The Manufacturers Life Insurance Company has reduced its stake in The Kroger Co. by 8%, selling 24,403 shares but still retaining over 281,000 shares valued at approximately $15.6 million. This reduction comes as Kroger reported second-quarter adjusted EPS that beat estimates, though revenue was slightly below expectations and the company lowered its full-year identical-sales outlook due to inflation and competition. Despite these challenges, management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 EPS guidance and the stock has an average analyst price target significantly higher than its current trading price.

items.title: Can Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) Turn Scale Into an Advantage?
items.summary: Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) is being assessed in the current macro environment, characterized by elevated energy costs, firm Treasury yields, and renewed inflation concerns. The article highlights that Fabrinet's business profile, focusing on operational scale, niche market share, margin discipline, and expansion across established end markets, positions it relevantly within the Midcap Stocks sector. The discussion emphasizes how the company's execution and business mechanics are critical in navigating volatile input costs, uneven demand, and changing financial conditions, rather than relying solely on broad market sentiment.

items.title: Lululemon Stock Crashes – Is It Finally a Buy?
items.summary: Lululemon's stock has crashed by about 52% in 2026, reaching an eight-year low, but the company remains highly profitable and financially stable with a strong balance sheet. The article explores whether this downturn presents a buying opportunity or indicates a permanent decline in its brand advantage, particularly noting the impact of declining North American sales and increasing competition. Despite financial strength, the brand's long-term value hinges on its ability to reinvigorate product desirability and navigate unpredictable trade policies.

items.title: WINTON GROUP Ltd Has $1.64 Million Stock Position in Hanmi Financial Corporation $HAFC
items.summary: WINTON GROUP Ltd reduced its stake in Hanmi Financial Corporation (NASDAQ:HAFC) by 56% in the second quarter, selling 64,266 shares but still retaining 50,486 shares valued at $1.64 million. Institutional investors collectively own 88.66% of the company. Hanmi Financial reported Q2 EPS of $0.79, beating estimates, but revenue of $72.21 million missed analyst expectations, and the company maintains a quarterly dividend of $0.28 per share.

items.title: Colgate-Palmolive is considering the sale of the Softsoap, Irish Spring, and Speed Stick brands in a transaction worth over one billion dollars
items.summary: Colgate-Palmolive is exploring the sale of its Softsoap, Irish Spring, and Speed Stick brands, a transaction estimated to exceed $1 billion, and has engaged Goldman Sachs to manage the process. This move is part of a broader industry trend where major consumer goods companies streamline their portfolios and focus on core brands due to economic pressures. While its personal care division contributed 17% of 2025 net sales, oral care remains Colgate-Palmolive's primary business.
